title: Straighten a leaning tabletop Christmas tree in its three-eye-bolt stand: ease one bolt out as the other screws in
instruction: Straighten the little Christmas tree in its stand so that it stands upright and firm.
context: A real Christmas tree goes into an eye-bolt stand in millions of homes each December (about 21.6 million real trees were bought in the US in 2023), and getting it to stand straight is the part people dread: the Real Christmas Tree Board calls the classic eye-bolt stand a two-person job. Here the tree is already gripped by all three bolts but leans 2.5 degrees. The trunk is caged, so it cannot be pushed upright, and screwing in the bolt on the lean side alone just jams against the other two: the bolt opposite must be eased out while the lean-side bolt goes in, by matched amounts (about 3.5 turns of each fine thread, regripping each eye every half turn), until the tree is plumb with every bolt still on the bark.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. Tree stand (Jack-Post Oasis 313-ST: green polypropylene, 33 cm (13 in) across the base, 17.8 cm (7 in) tall; fixed to the table, reservoir empty) centred at (34, 0): a bowl tapering to 24 cm across at its deck 10 cm up, and on it a collar 15.6 cm across with a 12.7 cm (5 in) opening, through which three zinc-plated steel 5/16 in-18 eye bolts point at the centre, 15 cm up: A at 120 degrees from +x (front left), B at 240 degrees (front right), C at 0 degrees (back). Each bolt: eye 26 mm across of 6 mm wire, 80 mm from the eye to its steel end cap (15 mm across, 9 mm long); 1.411 mm a turn, clockwise from outside screws it in. Centre spike tip 2 cm up. Tree: fresh-cut 3 ft tabletop fir, 91 cm tall from the butt, 1.5 kg, trunk 45 mm across and bare for 30 cm above the butt, foliage 43 cm across at the bottom; butt on the spike. Start: all three end caps on the bark and the trunk leaning 2.5 degrees towards +y (top about 4 cm off), the caps' faces 27.6 mm (A), 17.8 mm (B) and 22.7 mm (C) from the stand's axis. Distractors (NVIDIA SimReady, loose): unlit pillar candle (decor_candle_a01, 7.4 cm across, 7.5 cm tall, 0.35 kg) at (50, 33); mug (dishware_mug_a01, 11.4 x 9 x 8 cm, 0.30 kg) at (48, -36), turned 138 degrees; notebook (misc_notebook_a01, 22.9 x 17 x 1 cm, 0.25 kg) at (66, -24), turned 100 degrees. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the trunk's tilt (real trial: a digital angle gauge on the bare trunk), each end cap's gap to the bark (a 1 mm feeler gauge) and the grippers' clearance (video). 1.0: the trunk within 1.0 degree of vertical, all three end caps bearing on the bark (gap at most 1 mm: the feeler will not pass), every fingertip point of both grippers (each finger's tip and 3 cm up it) at least 3 cm from the trunk below the branches and from all three eyes, and the tree still (turning under 0.02 rad/s), all held for 2 s. 0.5: at the end, the trunk within 1.0 degree of vertical with both grippers 3 cm clear, short of full credit (for example a cap not bearing). 0.25: at the end, all three caps bearing and both grippers clear, with the trunk within 2.0 degrees of vertical but more than 1.0. 0: anything else, including the starting 2.5 degree lean and a gripper still on the tree or a bolt. Letting the tree flop scores 0 for the whole trial: the trunk at any time more than 6 degrees from vertical.
reset_notes: Set the tree plumb with all three caps lightly on the bark (angle gauge 0.0 +-0.1 degrees on two faces), then turn A out and B in by equal half-turns, C untouched, until the gauge on the trunk's left face reads 2.5 +-0.2 degrees with all three caps on the bark (a 1 mm feeler passes at none): about 3.5 turns each, about 2 minutes. Put the distractors back on their marks. Nothing is consumed; replace the tree if it sheds needles or its bark is crushed at the caps (trunk 44 to 46 mm across at the bolts).
fidelity: Full size, no rescaling: 3 ft tree; stand at its listed 13 x 7 in with 5 in opening (profile reconstructed). Trunk pivots on the spike (two hinges), cannot lift out; foliage seen only (branches bend aside). Bolt threads are code: 1.411 mm/turn, no back-drive, a snug bolt stops turning (90 N); caps push 300 N at most. Tree mass 1.5 kg estimated. Stand fixed, reservoir empty. Rigid bark, blunt caps. Tree, stand, bolts custom meshes; distractors SimReady.
